correctness.rationale: For each petal, forbidding a (-,+) consecutive orientation sign pair exhausts local valid forms: two directed cycles or l-1 source-to-sink orientations. Hub indegree requires at least one cyclic petal. A total dominating set must include the hub, l-3 nonhubs per outward petal and l-2 nonhubs per cyclic petal, plus one cyclic terminal incoming to the hub. The constructive choices show equality. The resulting product weights count each distinct edge orientation once. Finite brute-force subset and orientation enumeration confirms coefficients on eight length tuples, including 4096 orientations for (3,4,5).

evidence: Anderson et al. give exact upper/lower values for unicyclic graphs and a girth-restricted classification, not a multi-cycle orientation enumerator.
Blázsik–Nagy characterize graphs with upper number equal to their order minus one; for t=2 the present upper endpoint agrees with that class-wide result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A bouquet with t>=2 independent cycle petals has t cycles, so the unicyclic theorem is inapplicable. The 2024 extremal characterization covers scalar upper values when t=2, but for t>2 the upper endpoint is |V|-t+1 and even in t=2 its theorem does not determine coefficients, lower values, or full orientation multiplicities.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior general bounds and a special fan construction cannot determine exact orientation counts for multi-cycle bouquets. The 2024 scalar two-petal upper case is explicitly excluded from novelty in isolation. The polynomial also verifies interval realization for every bouquet by positive coefficients.

originality.rationale: Distinct from the 1999 invariant definition, the 2023 unicyclic and grid/complete-bipartite results, and the 2024 characterization restricted to the upper endpoint |V|-1. The present factorized polynomial determines the entire distribution for t>=2 vertex-amalgamated cycles. The later theorem overlaps only the upper scalar case t=2. Source-level search and comparison were performed; unindexed earlier arguments remain a risk.

value.rationale: The theorem computes a full coefficientwise distribution on a natural infinite multicylclic cactus class, not just endpoint bounds. Its factors identify all valid local orientation types and imply every intermediate total-domination value is realized. It fills the nonunicyclic family-level gap left by the 2023 scalar analysis and provides information beyond the t=2 upper-extremal classification.
